interpretation: BRAF p.V600E is a well-established oncogenic driver mutation in NSCLC. Dabrafenib + trametinib (BRAF/MEK inhibitor combination) is FDA-approved for BRAF V600E-mutant NSCLC based on the BRF113928 trial. Response rates ~64%, median PFS 10.9 months.
evidence_summary: FDA-approved targeted therapy available (dabrafenib + trametinib). Level A evidence. Clinical trial BRF113928 demonstrated significant ORR and PFS benefit. COSMIC hotspot.

version_history.interpretation: BRAF p.V600E is a well-established oncogenic driver mutation.

interpretation: KRAS p.G12D is a common oncogenic mutation in NSCLC. No FDA-approved KRAS G12D-specific therapy is currently available. KRAS G12C inhibitors (sotorasib, adagrasib) are not active against G12D. Clinical trials with pan-KRAS inhibitors are ongoing (e.g. RMC-9805, MRTX1133).
evidence_summary: No FDA-approved therapy for G12D specifically. Active clinical trial landscape. KRAS G12C inhibitors not applicable. Consider trial eligibility.

interpretation: KRAS p.G12C is targetable with FDA-approved covalent KRAS G12C inhibitors. Sotorasib (CodeBreaK 100) and adagrasib (KRYSTAL-1) are both FDA-approved for previously treated KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC. Sotorasib ORR 37%, adagrasib ORR 43%.
evidence_summary: FDA-approved targeted therapies available (sotorasib, adagrasib). Level A evidence. Distinct from G12D — codon-specific therapy.

interpretation: ERBB2 (HER2) amplification is an established oncogenic alteration across solid tumours. Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) has pan-tumour FDA approval for HER2-amplified solid cancers (DESTINY-PanTumor02). Response depends on IHC/FISH co-testing. In breast/gastric, higher evidence level.
evidence_summary: Pan-tumour FDA approval for T-DXd (DESTINY-PanTumor02). IHC/FISH co-testing recommended. Tier depends on tumour type — breast/gastric may warrant Tier 1.

interpretation: EML4-ALK fusion is the prototypical ALK rearrangement in NSCLC. First-line alectinib (ALEX trial) or brigatinib (ALTA-1L) are preferred. Lorlatinib is active for brain metastases and acquired resistance. All ALK inhibitors require the ALK kinase domain to be in-frame from the 3' partner.
evidence_summary: Multiple FDA-approved ALK inhibitors (crizotinib, ceritinib, alectinib, brigatinib, lorlatinib). Alectinib preferred first-line (ALEX). Consider brain metastasis status for lorlatinib selection.
